verdict.rationale: OpenRouter documents endpoints for programmatically creating and managing its own API keys so apps can distribute or rotate them. A community user confirms that minting keys with per-key expiry and limits is easy, and BYOK means provider keys sit behind OpenRouter rather than in client code. However, team-level scoping of keys is not explicitly documented; workspaces appear only in the context of budgets, and nothing states outright that provider keys are never exposed to key holders. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-team/per-app key scoping or workspace-bound key assignment, an explicit statement that BYOK provider keys stay hidden from downstream key holders, and hands-on corroboration beyond one community comment.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can mint gateway-managed keys for teams and apps without exposing raw provider keys

citations.quote: OpenRouter provides endpoints to programmatically manage your API keys, enabling key creation and management for applications that need to distribute or rotate keys automatically.
One thing that OpenRouter makes easy is the ability to manage API keys (mint new ones, expiry/limits per key, etc.)
OpenRouter supports both OpenRouter credits and the option to bring your own provider keys (BYOK)
